decision: Size the batch from measured end-to-end tool latency, not the declared 115000 ms: with a measured ~5.0s constant hidden cost per click plus explicit waits plus screenshot-hang risk, a 115 s budget cannot contain the recorded burst — cap clicks per cell (recorded safe bound: 12 or fewer), never wrap two game weeks into one cell, skip screenshots on animation/dialogue frames, or equivalently raise the declared timeout to the measured estimate. After a mid-business-sequence timeout, treat the entire in-flight sequence's outcome as UNKNOWN, reconcile from the next fresh stable state against the validated durable record, and retry nothing until reconciliation completes.
facts: timeout_debug_report.json: two burst cells declared timeout_ms 115000 and both were aborted by the js tool timeout — the s2_w1+w2 two-week cell estimated ~56 clicks + 36s waits + screenshots at ~350s+ real runtime, and the s4_w1 cell estimated ~22 clicks + ~25s waits + up to 30s screenshot hang at ~165s real — both far above the declared 115s.

Measured runtime limits: each cua.click carries a constant ~5.0s hidden cost (measured 5008/5078/5095 ms, independent of page state; single-click minimal test 5016 ms PASS), screenshots have an internal 30000 ms timeout with static pages captured in under 2s but animation/dialogue frames able to hang to the cap, the js cell timeout cap is 120000 ms, and tabs not marked for handoff at turn end get released (once leaving zero tabs).

Recorded safe workarounds: keep each cell at 12 clicks or fewer (12×5s=60s) or compress the declared timeout to the measured estimate; never wrap two game weeks into one cell; take no screenshots during animation/dialogue frames (wait for an INPUT_READY frame); mark the game tab for handoff before every turn end.

GATES.md BATCH_EXECUTION_MUST_RESPECT_MEASURED_TOOL_LATENCY: size multi-action batches using measured end-to-end latency of the actual tool path, not only explicit waits or the logical action count; if the estimated duration approaches the execution budget, split the batch before execution.

WINGRUN_20260905_01 weekly trace records the mid-sequence interruption: the blind loop was aborted mid-execution in S2_W1 with the game state uncertain (possibly dialogue/lesson/HOME); the later recovery entry (RECOVERY_FROM_CHECKPOINT) reconciled fresh state — recovered page WING_HOME at weeks=4 against a stale checkpoint expectation (8 or 7), result OK because it matched the independently validated chain (weeks=4, gap=4610); the run resumed from S2_W5 per policy.

learned_constraints runtime candidate C1 (PROVISIONAL, n=1): after a post-action observation tool failure the pending transaction must be reconciled against the next fresh stable state before any retry of the pending action; an observation-tool failure must not be read as transaction-pending and must not trigger a blind re-click.
inferences: The declared 115000 ms was mis-sized because it ignored the measured ~5s-per-click hidden cost and screenshot-hang risk; a correct batch is sized as clicks × ~5s + explicit waits + worst-case screenshot time, and split whenever that total approaches the budget — exactly what the GATES batching invariant requires.

After a mid-batch timeout the already-executed prefix of the sequence may have committed weeks: its outcome is UNKNOWN until fresh stable evidence reconciles it; the recorded precedent resolved this by matching a fresh observation against the validated durable chain (the checkpoint itself was stale), then resuming per policy — not by re-running the batch.

Re-running the remaining sub-actions of an aborted batch before reconciliation risks double commitment; an observation or tool failure must never be converted into an assumption about the business transaction.
unknowns: Exactly which clicks of the aborted burst landed and which game transactions committed at abort time is UNKNOWN — the trace records the state as uncertain until reconciled.

Whether the ~5s hidden click cost is a fixed platform budget or configuration-dependent is suspected (implicit wait/acknowledgement budget) but not proven; screenshot-hang behavior varies with page motion and is not fully predictable.
Whether the 12-click bound generalizes beyond the recorded cells is not established.
reason: The records show 115000 ms cannot hold the recorded burst once the measured ~5s/click hidden cost, waits, and screenshot-hang risk are counted, so the batch must be sized from measured end-to-end latency and split per the GATES batching invariant — one game week per cell, screenshots only on INPUT_READY frames. After a mid-business-sequence timeout the in-flight outcome is UNKNOWN: reconcile from the next fresh stable state against the validated durable boundary before any retry — the recorded precedent reconciled (checkpoint stale, server matched the validated chain) and resumed per policy without re-running the batch.
